comment.content:
> Are you seeing your instance as a means to patiently persue a certain ideology rather than allowing free speech and open uninterupted and respectful discourse?

We have no obligation to platform pro-genocide, patriarchal, white supremacist, cissupremacist, homophobic, or otherwise oppressive speech, and more, we have a moral obligation to silence those bigoted groups, deprive them of their right to speak, and prevent them from spreading their harmful views, and not only for the mental health of our users, of whom many are members of those targeted groups, but because we know that its the modus operandi of these white-supremacist/bigoted groups to set up nazi bars on social media platforms to spread their views, get people to associate and agree with them, and grow. The correct answer has always been, and remains, to deny them a platform.

If other servers, following the line of reddit and other US social media companies, want to platform those views to increase ragebait engagement and their user counts, there's nothing we can do about that, but at least here we can think about the long-term mental health of our users, which is far more important than user counts.

Fediverse instances are like email servers, if they call something spam and don't want to host it, then that's their prerogative. Arguments for "free speech" do not require them to host what you want them to host.

We also don't buy the [liberal notion of "free speech"](https://www.reddit.com/r/communism101/comments/c9ee36/comment/et0a5tc/), and think that even if there was such a thing, liberal countries and spaces don't actually practice it. Much like all liberal countries have a long history of banning anti-capitalist / anti-imperialist speech, organizing, and communist political parties, the instance you're on also doesn't adhere to "free and open speech": they've blocked the most popular leftist instances in the fediverse (hexbear and lemmygrad), to shield their userbase from those views. 

> I don’t understand why we need this division, and though you decry it in your comment, through actions or inactions, communities and moderators on your instance are allowed to amplify this division.

We have a *be respectful* rule here, and we do enforce it with temp bans, however it is unavoidable that some people (especially when venturing outside of lemmy.ml), encounter extremely bigoted and pro-genocide takes, and that makes them understandably angry. Still, if you see people from our instance breaking that rule, then report it, and we'll get to it when we can.

> How come you seem to allow communities who are moderated by a single user who repeatedly bans people just because they don’t like what someone says in an instant?

> To be instant banned for a few paragraphs. Then being name called by that mod, in a community without any rules, and then being banned with the reason ‘Zionist’ while I am just about 180º the opposite is not the way to persuade people like me. 

I don't know the circumstances, so you'd have to be more specific, linking examples. We made the modlog public, and its possible to link to every modded item to see what happened.

> I listed the challenges, how hard it was to communicate, how I was past the point of all hope to see it ever improving. Then the person said to me: “Good. So what are _you_ going to do about it?”

Despite ideological differences, and some loud users on other servers demanding more defederations, we actually have good relations with most other fediverse server admins and runners. We don't make demands on each other, each server has full autonomy to take mod actions on both local and federated users, and that autonomy is respected.

post.name: [.ml users] How would describe your instance?
post.body:
I might get hate because of my instance here, but in an attempt to better understand Lemmy I’m wondering if some of you can shed a light on why you chose this instance, what’s great about it, what could be better, is the instance rivalries something that affects your use of the platform or is it just background noise?

I’m not trying to start a fight or mud slinging, it would be good if several people could say their piece and nobody shame or attack them for it no matter how much you disagree.

comment.content:
> is people making assumptions about other's beliefs based soley on their instance of choice. It's not helpful, it's not generative, and it's a waste of everyone's time.

Spot on. Taking countries as an analogy for fediverse instances, we shouldn't make all the citizens of those countries into an ideological monolith: there's always a diversity of views, even if some views are more predominant than others because they're encouraged from the top. 

And above all we should not be alienating and unecessarily divisive to those who, with a little education and prodding in the right direction, will side with the majority of the world's workers. Our job is to make allies, patiently educate, and create more caring people.

post.name: Brazil’s Lula wins electoral court challenge against Meta for alleged pro-Bolsonaro algorithm bias
post.body:
SÃO PAULO — A judge of Brazil’s top electoral court ruled Thursday that Meta must adopt measures to immediately secure equal treatment of the two presidential candidates ahead of an Oct. 25 runoff.

The ruling comes shortly after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is running against Flávio Bolsonaro, filed a complaint that accused the tech company that owns Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp of using biased algorithms and AI restrictions to favor opposition candidate Bolsonaro ahead of the election.

Lula’s campaign argues that accounts and advertisements associated with Flávio Bolsonaro have reportedly received artificially inflated visibility, with engagement metrics rivaling those of global celebrities. The two are in a close race for the presidency, after the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro garnered 47% of the vote against 45% for the incumbent in the first round on Oct. 4.

post.name: Lemmy Development Update September 2026
post.body:
This last month, we've been working on Oauth fixes, various security fixes in the lemmy back-end, and a few front end fixes. We've also been working on [Jerboa](https://github.com/LemmyNet/jerboa) (our android app), to get it compatible with the new `1.0` API.

We're still readying the `1.0` release, which you can keep track of by watching the milestones below:

- https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/milestone/24
- https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/milestone/5
- https://github.com/LemmyNet/jerboa/milestone/1

Here are all the changes from September:

::: spoiler Full list of changes by repo

## lemmy

- [Remove redundant person_id indexes from smoosh-tables-together migration](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/pull/6661) by @dullbananas
- [Improve error message for OauthLoginFailed (ref #6609)](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/pull/6675) by @Nutomic
- [Validate the followers_url in the apub verify.](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/pull/6673) by @dessalines

- [Bind correct `this` handles in modal mixin](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/pull/4320) by @Nutomic
- [Fixing create post button.](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/pull/4319) by @dessalines
- [Add modlog filters for warnings](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/pull/4310) by @Nutomic
- [Fix for ViewerJS leak](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/pull/4305) by @Nutomic

## joinlemmy-site

## jerboa

:::

Or see the full list of changes at the links below: 

- [Backend](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy/pulls?q=merged%3A2026-09-01..2026-09-30+sort%3Acomments-desc)
- [Frontend](https://github.com/LemmyNet/lemmy-ui/pulls?q=merged%3A2026-09-01..2026-09-30+-author%3Aapp%2Frenovate+sort%3Acomments-desc)
- [join-lemmy.org](https://github.com/LemmyNet/joinlemmy-site/pulls?q=merged%3A2026-09-01..2026-09-30+-author%3Aapp%2Frenovate+sort%3Acomments-desc)
- [Jerboa](https://github.com/LemmyNet/jerboa/pulls?q=merged%3A2026-09-01..2026-09-30+-author%3Aapp%2Frenovate+sort%3Acomments-desc)

---

An open source project the size of Lemmy needs constant work to manage the project, implement new features and fix bugs. Dessalines and Nutomic work full-time on these tasks and more. As there is no advertising or tracking, all of our work is funded through donations. Even so there is barely enough time in the day, and no time for a second job. The only available option are user donations.

To keep it viable donations need to reach a minimum of 5000€ per month, resulting in a modest salary of 2500€ per developer. If that goal is reached we can stop worrying about money, and fully focus on improving the software for the benefit of all users and instances. We especially rely on recurring donations to secure the long-term development and make Lemmy the best it can be.

[Donate](https://join-lemmy.org/donate)

post.name: GitHub - dessalines/qbit-pause: A library for qBittorrent to pause popular torrents
post.body:
Pausing popular torrents isn't something that qBittorrent handles well. This library uses 2 criteria to pause / stop torrents.

They are stopped if they are:

- Popular (IE have a lot of total seeds)
- You've given back more than what you've taken (IE a seed ratio > 1)

This library

## Requirements

- Rust
- A qBittorrent server.
- An API key generated through the web UI.
- A crontab where this script can be periodically run.

## Usage

This will pause torrents with a ratio >= 2, and more than 10 total seeds.

```sh
cargo run -- \
--api-key API_KEY \
--endpoint ENDPOINT \
--ratio 2 \
--total-seeds 10
```
